web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Ten Years of Financial Forensics — Margins, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet Fortress
question: Do TSMC's 10-year audited numbers confirm self-funded compounding, or is $60B+ annual capex eroding free cash flow and return on invested capital?

epigraph.quote: Capital intensity is only a curse when returns fall below the cost of capital; when ROIC clears 24% to 32%, capex is the moat.
epigraph.author: Institutional Forensic Principle

web_blocks.text: 10-Year P&L, Cash Flow & Capital Intensity Trajectory (FY2016–YTD 2026)
web_blocks.title: 10-Year P&L, Cash Flow & Capital Intensity Trajectory (FY2016–YTD 2026)

web_blocks.html: From FY2016 through FY2025, TSMC grew USD revenue more than fourfold from $29.43 billion to $122.42 billion (~17.2% 9-year CAGR) [2, 20]. Gross margin expanded nearly 10 points from 50.1% to 59.9%. Annual free cash flow grew nearly fivefold from ~$6.5 billion to $31.99 billion [2, 20]. Momentum accelerated in 2026: Q1–Q3 2026 revenue reached ~$122.8 billion, matching all of FY2025 in nine months [3, 4, 5]. Q3 2026 delivered 66.4% gross margin and 58.7% operating margin, with Q4 2026 sales guided to $52.3B–$54.3B [5].

web_blocks.caption: TSMC 10-Year Financial Forensics (FY2016–FY2025 + Q1–Q3 2026, USD Billions)
web_blocks.takeaway: TSMC generated positive free cash flow in all ten years, including 2019, 2023, and the $40.6B FY2025 capex surge. Operating cash flow exceeded net income by 132% to 187% through FY2025, easing to 117.6% in 9M 2026 as receivables and inventories expanded [21].

web_blocks.text: Balance Sheet Fortress, Working Capital & ROIC vs. WACC
web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Fortress, Working Capital & ROIC vs. WACC

web_blocks.html: TSMC spent $136.6 billion in cumulative capex from FY2021 to FY2025, yet its balance sheet remains a net-cash fortress [20]. On December 31, 2025, TSMC held NT$3,068,594 million (~US$97.6 billion) in cash and liquid instruments [8]. That total includes NT$2,767,856M in cash equivalents and NT$300,738M in current marketable securities [8]. Total debt stood at just NT$993,154 million (~US$31.7 billion), split between NT$136,926M current and NT$856,228M non-current bonds [8]. Net cash sits near US$66 billion, backed by a 2.58x current ratio, 2.37x quick ratio, and 0.15x Debt-to-Equity (LT Debt/Eq 0.12x). By September 30, 2026, cash and current marketable securities expanded to NT$4,016.72 billion (~US$126.00 billion)—comprising NT$3,621.89B in cash equivalents and NT$394.83B in current debt investments—against NT$1,031.58 billion (~US$32.36 billion) in total debt, lifting net cash to US$93.64 billion [21]. In 9M 2026, operating cash flow of NT$2,402.12B easily funded NT$1,289.97B in PP&E capex to generate NT$1,112.15B (~US$34.9 billion) in free cash flow [21].

Working capital discipline reinforces cash conversion. DSO improved from 34.3 days in FY2024 to 27.0 days in FY2025, while DIO tightened from 82.7 days to 68.8 days [16]. Operating cash flow converted at 132.4% of Net Income ($72.52B CFO vs. $54.76B Net Income at year-end FX) thanks to $21.94B in non-cash depreciation [1, 11]. ROIC climbed from 20.0% in FY2024 to 24.6% in FY2025 and 32.67% TTM in the Nov 2026 snapshot [16]. ROE rose from 27.3% to 31.7% in FY2025 (41.98% TTM), clearing an ~8%–9% cost of capital by 15 to 23 points [16]. Share count stayed flat (~5.19B ADR equivalents / ~25.9B common shares) with zero dilution while funding a growing cash dividend (25.98% payout ratio). Over the full FY2016–FY2025 arc, cumulative operating cash flow easily outpaced $136.6 billion in FY2021–FY2025 capital spending, proving that TSMC's cleanest fabs are self-funded [20]. Even as FY2026 capex rises to $60B–$64B, 2.58x current liquidity and 28.93% ROA confirm exceptional asset productivity [4, 8].

web_blocks.text: Depreciation-to-Capex Cycle, Customer Prepayments & Capital Allocation
web_blocks.title: Depreciation-to-Capex Cycle, Customer Prepayments & Capital Allocation

web_blocks.html: Understanding TSMC's cash engine requires tracking the 10-year depreciation-to-capex cycle. Annual capex climbed from ~$10.0B–$10.8B in FY2016–FY2017 to $30.04B–$36.56B in FY2021–FY2022 and $40.56B–$40.90B in FY2025, before guiding $60B–$64B for FY2026 [1, 4, 20]. Because TSMC depreciates fab tools straight-line over five years, FY2025 depreciation and amortization reached NT$688,096 million ($21.94B) [11]. That non-cash expense explains why FY2025 operating cash flow ($72.52B) converted at 132.4% of GAAP net income ($54.76B) [1, 11]. As older N7 and N5 equipment rolls off its five-year schedule, legacy nodes throw off higher cash margins that help fund N2 and A16 ramps.

TSMC also pairs commercial capacity locks with evolving capital deployment. Multi-year long-term agreements (LTAs) and customer deposits back leading-edge and CoWoS cleanrooms before tools arrive [1, 14]. TSMC still avoids large dilutive M&A and keeps share count flat at ~5.19B ADR equivalents (~25.9B common shares) [16]. However, on November 10, 2026, the Board authorized up to US$1.5 billion in strategic AI ecosystem equity stakes: up to US$500M in Anthropic, PBC at IPO, up to US$500M in OpenAI Group PBC preferred stock, and up to US$500M for a semiconductor investment subsidiary [23]. Alongside a 28.6% Q3 cash dividend hike to NT$9.0 per share [23], these AI customer stakes remain small against US$93.64B in net cash yet add modest circular-demand exposure.

web_blocks.text: Footnote Forensics: Customer Deposits, Grant Deductions & Governance Alignment
web_blocks.title: Footnote Forensics: Customer Deposits, Grant Deductions & Governance Alignment

web_blocks.html: Working Capital Divergence, Temporary Receipts & Grant Masking. Q3 2026 footnotes reveal three cash-quality nuances missed by headline ratios [21]. First, Note 20c shows temporary receipts from customers nearly doubled from NT$189.86 billion at year-end 2025 to NT$359.48 billion (~US$11.3 billion) on September 30, 2026 [21]. That balance splits into NT$231.95B current and NT$127.53B noncurrent deposits, alongside NT$54.14B in contract liabilities and NT$79.29B in FY2025 refund liabilities [1, 21]. Because these deposits enter CFO (+NT$229.43B from other noncurrent liabilities in 9M 2026) and may be refunded or offset against receivables, they flatter peak-cycle cash conversion [21]. Second, accounts receivable jumped +NT$196.26B (with select receivables factored without recourse under Note 11) and inventories climbed +NT$139.64B, pulling 9M 2026 CFO/NI down from 132.4% in FY2025 to 117.6% [21]. Third, Q2 2026 earnings included a NT$63.20 billion gain from selling 8.1% of Vanguard International Semiconductor (VIS), driven largely by a non-cash fair-value remeasurement of the remaining 19% stake [21]. Meanwhile, NT$167.59B in 9M government grants offset carrying PP&E and lowered GAAP depreciation [21].

Governance Incentives, Statutory Commitments & Insider Alignment. Under TSMC's Articles of Incorporation (Note 27), employee profit-sharing is at least 1% of annual profits (accruing NT$112.32 billion in 9M 2026, +54.4% YoY; key management pay NT$8.46 billion) [21]. Note 33 also records a standing 1987 ITRI agreement permitting the R.O.C. government to utilize up to 35% of capacity without prejudicing customer commitments (never invoked), plus a 28%–70% capacity take-or-pay floor on Singapore JV SSMC [21]. Favorably, October and November 2026 insider filings confirm zero executive share pledges and continued net share accumulation by CEO C.C. Wei, CFO Wendell Huang, senior executives, and board directors [26, 27].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Verdict on Capital Intensity
paragraphs: TSMC passes its core cash-generation tests: ten straight years of positive FCF (~$34.9B in 9M 2026), FY2016–FY2025 CFO/NI of 132%–187% moderating to 117.6% in 9M 2026, $93.64B gross net cash (~$82.3B ex-NT$359.48B refundable customer temporary receipts, up from ~$66B at year-end 2025), flat shares, and 24.6%–32.67% ROIC [16, 21].

Four financial watch items require ongoing tracking: (1) $60B–$64B FY2026 capex creating 2027–2028 depreciation drag if AI demand cools, (2) NT$167.59B in 9M PP&E grant deductions flattering GAAP depreciation and ROIC, (3) Q2's NT$63.20B non-cash VIS remeasurement gain, and (4) up to $1.5B in AI customer equity stakes [4, 21, 23].

book_paragraphs: Numbers never lie over a full ten-year arc. Laying TSMC's audited income statements, cash flows, and balance sheets from 2016 through 2025—plus nine months of 2026—side by side reveals one clear truth. This is one of the rarest industrial compounding machines ever built.

From 2016 to 2025, TSMC grew USD sales from $29.43 billion to $122.42 billion. Gross margins rose from 50.1% to 59.9% (and 66.4% in Q3 2026), while free cash flow jumped from $6.5 billion to $31.99 billion. Even better, TSMC posted positive free cash flow every single year, including the 2019 smartphone lull, the 2023 downturn, and the 2025 capex surge.

A great business must prove itself in cash flow and balance-sheet health. Across FY2016 through FY2025, TSMC's compounding record is extraordinary, with USD sales quadrupling to $122.42 billion (+35.9% YoY in FY25). Unlike peers that burn cash while expanding, TSMC delivered ten straight years of positive FCF, hitting $31.96B–$31.99B in FY2025 after $40.5B+ in capex.

Cash conversion and working capital discipline remain strong, though Q3 2026 footnotes add important nuance. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow hit NT$2,402.12 billion (~$75.3 billion), or 117.6% of net income, generating NT$1,112.15 billion (~$34.9 billion) in free cash flow after NT$1,289.97 billion in PP&E outlays. On the balance sheet, cash and current securities grew to NT$4,016.72 billion (~$126.0 billion) against NT$1,031.58 billion (~$32.4 billion) in debt, lifting net cash to $93.64 billion by September 30, 2026.

A ten-year look at capex and depreciation shows why TSMC's cash flow stays resilient. Annual capital spending stepped up from roughly $10 billion in 2016 to $40.6 billion in 2025 and $60B–$64B in 2026. Because TSMC depreciates equipment straight-line over five years, FY2025 non-cash depreciation hit $21.94 billion.

That accounting conservatism powers 132.4% operating cash flow conversion against net income. Once N7 and N5 tools finish their five-year depreciation window, those mature lines generate rich cash margins that help self-fund the next wave of N2 and A16 cleanrooms.

This ten-year cash flow record also answers the classic bear critique about semiconductor capital intensity. From FY2016 through FY2025, TSMC never posted a single year of negative free cash flow. Even during the 2023 industry downturn and the 2025 capex surge, operating cash flow comfortably covered every dollar of fab construction.

book_callouts.title: A Net-Cash Fortress in a Capital-Intensive Industry
book_callouts.text: After spending over $136 billion on fabs from 2021 to 2025, TSMC ended 2025 with ~$66 billion in net cash. By September 30, 2026, gross net cash reached $93.64 billion (~$82.3 billion excluding NT$359.48 billion in customer temporary receipts) with Debt-to-Equity at 0.15x.

book_subsections.title: Why ROIC Clears the Hurdle Rate by 20+ Points
paragraphs: Critics worry that TSMC's $60B–$64B capex budget in 2026 will crush free cash flow. That is a fair concern, and we track it closely. Yet operating cash flow converts at 132% to 187% of net income because $21.9 billion in annual depreciation is a non-cash charge on tools that keep printing high-margin wafers.

That cash engine drove ROIC from 20.0% in 2024 to 24.6% in 2025 and 32.67% TTM in late 2026, while ROE hit 41.98%. Share count stayed flat at 5.19 billion ADR equivalents with zero dilution. Every forensic check confirms that TSMC's capex widens its moat rather than eroding value.

book_subsections.title: Why Financial Forensics Warrant COMPOUNDER_PASS
paragraphs: Combine 117.6% 9M 2026 CFO-to-net-income conversion, ten straight years of positive FCF, 24.6% FY2025 ROIC (32.67% TTM in 2026), and a $93.64 billion net cash cushion as of September 2026. Still, forensic rigor flags three footnote nuances to monitor. Temporary customer capacity deposits nearly doubled to NT$359.48 billion (flattering CFO), while NT$167.59 billion in 9M government grants reduced carrying PP&E and depreciation. In addition, Q2 2026 earnings included a NT$63.20 billion VIS gain driven largely by non-cash remeasurement.

That completes our price-blind audit of the business. On fundamentals alone, TSMC earns an unambiguous `COMPOUNDER_PASS`. With business conviction anchored in audited facts rather than market narratives, we are now ready to examine valuation.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Fortress and Capital Return Discipline
paragraphs: TSMC expanded its liquidity from ~$66 billion in net cash at year-end 2025 to $93.64 billion in gross net cash by September 30, 2026 (~$82.3 billion excluding NT$359.48 billion in customer temporary receipts). Even during a $60B–$64B capex cycle, operating cash flow funds both cleanrooms and a growing dividend.

TSMC avoids large dilutive M&A, though capital deployment broadened modestly on November 10, 2026. Alongside a 28.6% dividend hike to NT$9.0 per share and $40.93 billion in new capex approvals, the Board authorized up to $1.5 billion in strategic AI stakes: $500 million each for Anthropic at IPO, OpenAI preferred shares, and a semiconductor ecosystem fund. That marks a minor circular-financing shift worth watching, even if small beside $93.64 billion in net cash and zero insider share pledges.
Dividend growth reflects that cash discipline. TSMC raised its cash dividend at a 25.39% three-year rate and 14.54% five-year rate while keeping the payout ratio at a conservative 25.98%.

book_subsections.title: Customer Prepayments, LTAs, and Dividend Capital Allocation
paragraphs: TSMC does not build $20 billion GigaFabs on blind faith. Management pairs heavy capex with multi-year long-term capacity agreements and upfront customer prepayments on leading-edge and CoWoS lines, locking in demand before tools arrive.

On the balance sheet, $97.6 billion in cash and securities against $31.7 billion in debt gives TSMC a 0.15x debt-to-equity ratio and a 2.58x current ratio. With zero M&A distraction and a flat 5.19 billion ADR share count, every dollar of surplus cash compounds cleanroom scale and a steady dividend.

Working capital velocity adds another layer of protection. Between FY2024 and FY2025, days sales outstanding dropped from 34.3 days to 27.0 days while inventory days tightened from 82.7 days to 68.8 days. Faster customer collections and leaner wafer-in-process buffers convert booming HPC demand into immediate cash on the balance sheet.

book_subsections.title: Depreciation Schedules and Margin Durability
paragraphs: TSMC depreciates fab equipment aggressively, typically straight-line over five years. As a result, accounting gross margins already absorb heavy non-cash charges during ramp years. Once a node passes that five-year window, as N7 and N5 are doing, cash flow margins expand further.
That conservative policy means TSMC's 57.78% operating margin and 51.52% net margin are not flattered by stretched accounting. If anything, they understate the long-term cash power of each wafer fab.

Across 2016 to 2025, depreciation lagged rising capex during buildout surges, keeping CFO-to-net-income conversion between 132% and 187%. In 9M 2026, higher receivables and inventory moderated conversion to 117.6%, while NT$167.59 billion in cash government grants offset PP&E and flattered GAAP depreciation and ROIC.

For long-term investors, $93.64 billion in gross net cash (~$82.3 billion ex-customer deposits) changes the risk profile even as watch items grow. Monitoring FY2026 $60B–$64B capex, Q2's NT$63.20 billion non-cash VIS gain, and $1.5 billion in AI equity stakes keeps capital discipline transparent.

book_subsections.title: Cash Flow Durability Across Upcycles and Downturns
paragraphs: What sets TSMC apart in this 10-year audit is trough-cycle resilience, not just peak profits. During the 2023 inventory downturn when sales fell 8.7%, gross margin held at 54.4% and free cash flow stayed positive. That proves TSMC's pricing power is structural rather than an AI boom artifact.
Few hardware makers on earth can self-fund $30B to $60B in annual capex without tapping high-yield debt or diluting shareholders.
